verdicts.reason: A keeps a clean banner flow (box, then headline and body, then CTA) with the CTA fully inside the panel and clear gaps. But the 48H ONLY badge is shrunk to an illegible pink speck under the body copy. B jams the headline's 'price' against the CTA pill, lets the CTA overhang the panel's right edge, and squashes the badge to an unreadable '48HONLY' on the panel's bottom-left edge.

A breaks the headline into 'Box fresh, half / price' with an orphaned word and leaves 'stock.' alone on its own line. Its CTA is tiny and buried bottom-right, and the oversized badge, straddling the panel edge, outweighs it. B keeps the headline on one line with a prominent CTA, but the headline collides with the CTA, the CTA overflows the panel, and the badge is illegible.

A has the cleanest type hierarchy and a well-placed CTA. But it shrinks the VOLTSTRIDE box, the brand and hero product, plus the 48H badge into microscopic icons in the bottom corner, so the brand and key imagery are effectively lost. B keeps the product box readable but has the headline butting into the CTA, the CTA hanging off the panel, and a squashed, unreadable badge.
